<objective>
Deliver the shared-tablet staff session: the owner enables staff mode once on a physical device, which becomes a revocable, venue-scoped `staff` principal in the database (a provisioned device auth account with a `venue_members` role='staff' row), with a device registry, instant remote revoke, a real owner-unlock swap-back, and idle auto-relock. This is the ACCT-05 "staff sign in, see only their venues" mechanism and the second half of the ACCT-08 isolation matrix.

**User story (MVP):** **As a** restaurant owner, **I want to** turn a floor tablet into a trusted staff device that only sees my venue and that I can kill instantly if it is lost, **so that** staff can work from a shared device without ever being able to reach another venue's data or stay logged in after I revoke them.

Purpose: The novel design of this phase — the DB "staff" is a device, not a person (D-06). It must be a real auth principal so it plugs into the same `get_venue_role()` helper with no special-casing, revocation (D-08) must be authoritative at the RLS layer, and owner-unlock (D-07) must have a concrete swap-back, not a documented hope.
Output: migration 0003 (venue_devices), enableStaffMode (with reconciliation + supersede) + revoke + owner-unlock swap-back Server Actions, device registry UI, idle relock, and client-SDK tests proving venue-scoped device access, instant revoke, and safe re-enrollment.

Requirements covered: ACCT-05, ACCT-08.
</objective>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| Owner tablet → enableStaffMode | Privileged device provisioning using the secret key |
| Device session → PostgREST | The tablet's staff principal issues real queries; RLS scopes it |
| App → secret key (admin.ts) | A leak is a full RLS bypass |
| Physical device → data | A lost/stolen tablet holds a long-lived session; an unattended owner-unlock session is high blast radius |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-04-01 | Information Disclosure | cross-venue device read (IDOR) | high | mitigate | Device gets a venue_members row for exactly one venue; RLS via get_venue_role; device-session test asserts zero Venue B rows |
| T-04-02 | Elevation of Privilege | secret key in client bundle | high | mitigate | admin client imported only server-side by actions/devices.ts; no NEXT_PUBLIC_ secret; tests use an inline service-role client; grep guard (D-24, Pitfall 3) |
| T-04-03 | Elevation of Privilege | stolen tablet retains access after revoke | high | mitigate | Revoke deletes venue_members row (RLS re-checks every query = instant) + admin.signOut global; revoke test asserts instant denial pre-JWT-expiry (D-08, Pitfall 5) |
| T-04-04 | Elevation of Privilege | device session inherits owner dashboard access, or unattended owner-unlock session | medium | mitigate | (tablet) route group isolated from (dashboard); device role strictly 'staff'; owner-unlock auto-relocks to PIN on idle (D-07) |
| T-04-05 | Spoofing | anonymous-auth broad `authenticated` role | medium | mitigate | Provisioned device account (not anonymous auth), so no is_anonymous special-casing gap (RESEARCH Anti-Pattern) |
| T-04-06 | Elevation of Privilege | orphan half-provisioned device principal | medium | mitigate | enableStaffMode reconciles partial failure + supersedes prior (venue,label) device; partial unique index enforces one active device per label |
</threat_model>
